1.name: Léandre Charbonneau
1.about: The projected No. 1 pick, Léandre Charbonneau is viewed by some scouts as a potentially generational talent. The 6'11" French phenom pairs elite length and athleticism with explosive finishing, three-point range and game-changing rim protection. His unusually complete two-way skill set gives him the foundation of a franchise-altering modern big.

2.name: Michael Cheeks
2.about: Michael Cheeks has been one of the biggest risers of the early draft process, building on his five-star pedigree with a breakout showing for Team USA at the FIBA U19 World Cup. His polished handle, pull-up shooting and difficult shot-making stood out against international competition, pushing the Louisville freshman firmly into the No. 2 conversation.

3.name: Kevin Carter
3.about: The No. 1 overall recruit in the country, Kevin Carter arrives at Kansas carrying legitimate star expectations. At 6'9" with a 7'3" wingspan, Carter overwhelms defenders with long strides, explosive finishing and rare physical tools for a wing. His jumper remains the swing skill separating an elite prospect from a potential franchise centerpiece.

4.name: Jan Zorko
4.about: Jan Zorko remains more projection than production after seeing limited minutes for Cedevita Olimpija, but his flashes have scouts calling him a potential unicorn. The 7-footer can protect the rim, handle in transition and initiate breaks himself. With a larger role expected this season, he could become the draft’s biggest riser.

5.name: Asafa Tinibu
5.about: Already projected as a top-five pick, Asafa Tinibu enters his sophomore season at Georgia with breakout expectations after an encouraging freshman campaign. The powerful 6'5" wing combines an explosive first step, length and relentless rim pressure with a college-ready frame. Scouts believe improved perimeter shooting could unlock another level offensively.

6.name: Awut Jok
6.about: Awut Jok is one of the draft’s biggest developmental swings, having started playing basketball only five years ago after growing up in South Sudan. Now the 7'2" Duke freshman flashes remarkable shooting touch and rim protection for his experience level. His limited mobility is concerning, but scouts believe he is only scratching the surface.

7.name: Nate Johnson
7.about: A top-10 recruit nationally, Nate Johnson arrives at Alabama with a reputation as one of the most gifted scorers in his class. The 6'8" forward combines strength, touch and polished footwork to create from the midrange and paint. His advanced scoring instincts give him immediate appeal as a high-end lottery prospect.

8.name: Josh Houston
8.about: The No. 2 recruit in the country, Josh Houston arrives at North Carolina with a reputation built on overwhelming physicality and explosive athleticism. The powerful 6'8" lefty dominates around the basket as a finisher and rebounder despite being undersized for center. Developing his perimeter skill set will determine his ultimate offensive ceiling.

9.name: Dremonte Johnson Jr.
9.about: Dremonte Johnson Jr. posted modest numbers as a Michigan freshman, but his efficiency and explosive flashes kept scouts intrigued. Now stepping into a substantially larger role, the 6'9" sophomore is expected to produce. His elite athleticism, violent finishing and defensive playmaking give him the tools to turn increased opportunity into a breakout season.

10.name: Gunnar Davies
10.about: After a breakout season at Creighton that earned him a top-eight finish in national Player of the Year voting, Gunnar Davies transfers to Duke with considerable expectations. The junior is an elite perimeter marksman with deep range and polished shot-making instincts. Proving himself against increased defensive attention could strengthen his lottery standing.
